To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aerobic exercise training plus weight loss improves skeletal muscle glycogen synthesis and glucose uptake in older men.
aerobic exercise plus weight loss increases insulin activation of skeletal muscles' glycogen synthase in older, overweight men.

6-month aerobic training + weight loss improves insulin activation of skeletal-muscle glycogen synthase (GlyS) activity and increases citrate synthase (CIT) activity, but does not alter Akt and AS160 (Akt substrate 160) phosphorylation, and that the improvement in GlyS fractional activity (FA) is associated with an increase in glucose utilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise on insulin action in older, obese men.
the effects of aging on skeletal muscle function.
the effects of aging and exercise on the regulation of glycogen synthases and the role of glycogen synthas in glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AEX + WL increases basal and insulin activation glycogen synthase in older men, and this may contribute to the improvement in whole body glucose utilization.
AEX + WL improves insulin sensitivity in older, insulin-resistant men by increasing basal and insulin activation skeletal muscle glycogen synthesis.
aerobic exercise plus weight loss (AER+WL) improves insulin sensitivity and glycogen synthase in older men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aerobic exercise training plus weight loss improves glucose utilization in older men by increasing insulin activation of skeletal glycogen synthase.
AEX + WL improves insulin sensitivity and skeletal muscle glycogen synthesis in older, overweight, and obese men.
AEX + WL increases skeletal muscle glucose transport capacity and glycogen synthesis capacity, and these changes are associated with improved glucose uptake and utilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aerobic exercise training plus weight loss improves glucose utilization in older men by increasing insulin activation of skeletal-muscle glycogen synthase.
the combination of aerobic exercise training and intentional weight loss is effective for improving insulin resistance in older adults.
exercise and weight loss can have a profound effect on improving insulin sensitivity in older men.
